summary: You choose a primary track (25 units) and a different secondary track (15 units), each allowing one pre-approved course from outside Political Science, and add POLISCI 1, a methods course, 20 units of additional coursework, a 5-unit 200- or 300-level seminar (which also counts toward a track or the additional units), a 5-unit WIM course and a capstone, for 70 units. Every course needs a letter grade of C or better unless it is offered only CR/S, and the audit applies the major's caps: 2 units of CR/S Political Science courses, two IntroSems or Sophomore College courses, 5 units of directed reading and 25 units from outside the department. Petitioned courses, the Interdisciplinary Honors capstone and honors eligibility are checked by hand.

cfaurZ3b.why: "Political Science majors must select a Primary and Secondary Track on which to focus their studies. They must complete at least 25 units of coursework toward the Primary Track and 15 units toward the Secondary Track. For the major, up to one course for the Primary Track and up to one course for the Secondary Track may be a pre-approved non-Political Science course or a petitioned course." The Bulletin data required all five tracks. Now one choice among the twenty primary/secondary pairs of different tracks: primary 25 units from its lists, secondary 15 units from its lists, each with at most one pre-approved non-POLISCI course. (A nested choice, primary then secondary, is not solved reliably by the audit's path search, so the pairs are listed flat.) Petitioned courses are moved in by hand. PHIL 175W is left out of the cap because it is cross-listed as POLISCI 137, which is on the POLISCI list.

9WgctjIx.why: "25 units in a primary Track and 15 units in a secondary Track." Encoded in the Depth in Discipline block (the track choice), so this line is information here.

U3j9XM4J.why: "Additional Coursework - 20 units": "Additional Political Science coursework, which may include any PoliSci courses regardless of track, pre-approved courses. This may include no more than 5 units of directed reading." Up to 20 units of honors coursework count here (POLISCI 299 is in the pool). The directed reading courses are POLISCI 219, 229, 239, 249, 259, 319 and 329. Policies: "Pre-approved and petitioned courses may count toward the additional coursework requirement." So every pre-approved course from another department named on this page (the track lists' non-POLISCI courses and the methods courses) is listed here too; the 25-unit cap on outside units still applies.

o3dx0uJm.why: "Students must take at least one 5-unit, 200-level or 300-level undergraduate seminar in Political Science. This course may count toward the units taken to satisfy the Primary Track, Secondary Track, or Additional Coursework requirements." Graduate-career listings are excluded as not undergraduate seminars; that a course is a seminar is not checked. Courses numbered below 200 whose cross-listing is a 200- or 300-level POLISCI number (POLISCI 150A is also 355A) are excluded, since the student takes them at the lower number.

y0vmWgtb.why: Block note: "WIM course must be taken for 5 units."

G4HsBIvd.why: "The Department of Political Science offers three capstone options: writing an honors thesis, completing a capstone project, or participating in a policy practicum." The Interdisciplinary Honors option has no text or courses in the Bulletin data, so it is marked met by hand.

ZELUt8iS.why: "Students pursuing the BAH are expected to complete the standard Political Science major as well as conduct research under the supervision of a faculty member, culminating in an honors thesis." The honors block is the opt-in; once in, POLISCI 299A-D are required, so the rule itself is not optional.

pb31Likb.why: "Honors Eligibility: GPA of 3.5 or higher ... Earn a grade of B or higher in POLISCI299A Research Design and POLISCI299B Honors Thesis Seminar ... The thesis must receive a grade of 'B+' or higher." Eligibility, application and grades are checked by hand.

PPlLLWah.why: Policies: "One pre-approved course may count toward the methods course requirement. STATS60, STATS101, ECON102A, CS106A, and CS 106B are courses outside the Political Science Department and count toward the 25-unit limit. POLISCI150A does not count toward the 25-unit limit." and "the Methods courses: CS106A, CS 106B, POLISCI150A, STATS60, STATS101". The rule's list leaves out STATS 101, which the policy text names twice as a methods course.

program.why: Grading: "All courses applied toward the major offered for a letter grade must be taken for a letter grade. All courses counting toward the major must receive a grade of 'C' or higher." A course offered only CR/S still counts with a CR or S.

totals.label: CR/S units in Political Science courses
totals.why: Grading: "Up to two units of Political Science courses that are not offered for a letter grade may be counted toward the major if completed for a CR or S grade."

totals.label: CR/S units in courses outside Political Science
totals.why: Grading: "Non-Political Science department classes not offered for a letter grade may not be applied to the major." The pre-approved courses from other departments are the ones named on this page. STATS 101 is a methods course the policies name.

totals.label: Introductory and Sophomore College seminars
totals.why: Policies: "No more than two 3-unit Stanford Introductory Seminar courses or Sophomore College courses can be applied toward the 70 unit major requirement." Read as 6 units of the department's N, Q and SC seminars numbered below 100.

totals.label: Directed reading
totals.why: Policies: "No more than 5 units of directed reading units may count toward the Political Science major."

totals.label: Units from outside Political Science
totals.why: Policies: "Students may count up to 25 units of coursework from outside the Political Science Department toward the Political Science major." Transfer: "Transfer credits, study abroad units, and courses from other departments at Stanford are all considered out-of-department units." Counted over the pre-approved courses from other departments named on this page (HISTORY 204G and PHIL 175W are left out because they are also POLISCI 104G and 137); petitioned courses are moved in by hand and not counted here. STATS 101 is a methods course the policies name.
